name: Modular Inc.
subcategory: AI compiler, programming language (Mojo) and inference platform (MAX, Modular Cloud)
origin_detail: Founded in 2022 by Chris Lattner (creator of LLVM and Swift) and Tim Davis, who met at Google; Silicon Valley HQ with offices in San Francisco, Los Altos, Boston and Edinburgh. Acquired by Qualcomm in July 2026.
flagship_projects: MAX (inference framework: graph compiler, runtime, kernels)
openness_notes: Initial 0: Mojo first appeared in May 2023 only as a hosted playground and MAX shipped as binaries, with no public source. Opened in stages: Mojo standard library in March 2024 (Apache-2.0 with LLVM exceptions); MAX's kernel library, Python APIs and models were Apache-2.0 before Oct 2026; the Mojo compiler and tooling went Apache-2.0 on 2026-08-18; on 2026-10-22 the rest of MAX (graph compiler, runtime, hardware backends) became source-available under a custom MAX License that is not OSI (no publishing modified source except contribution forks; no using MAX as AI input to reimplement it; a branding rule for hosted services). Current 2 (open core): the language and much of the stack are OSI-licensed, MAX's core is source-available, and revenue comes from the hosted Modular Cloud and enterprise deployments.

exit_events.note: Completion announced 2026-07-29 ('Qualcomm Completes Acquisition of Modular'); price $3.9B per Wikipedia's Qualcomm article; Modular's pages state no price. Qualcomm said Mojo, MAX and Modular Cloud continue as products and brands and that the open, heterogeneous-hardware approach continues.

risk_events: Jul 2026: acquired by chip maker Qualcomm; Modular says it will keep targeting NVIDIA, AMD and other silicon, but no binding hardware-neutrality commitment was found
Mar 2026: Modular dropped the goal of making Mojo a Python superset (forum post 16 Mar 2026)
Oct 2026: MAX's core is source-available only; the licence bars publishing modified source and using MAX as AI input to build a reimplementation
robustness: Mojo (compiler and standard library) is now Apache-2.0, so the language could survive or be forked without Modular; MAX's graph compiler and runtime are visible but not forkable under the MAX License. There is no foundation: governance sits with Modular, now a Qualcomm subsidiary.
physical_science_relevance: Mojo targets high-performance GPU and CPU kernels from Python-like code; an Oak Ridge National Laboratory study presented at SC25 found Mojo's GPU kernels broadly competitive with CUDA and HIP for memory-bound workloads, relevant to scientific computing.
openness_effect_assessment: Modular built most of its value while closed: its valuation reached $1.6B in Sep 2025 ('almost triple' the previous round) with Mojo's compiler and MAX's core proprietary. It opened step by step (2024 stdlib, Aug 2026 compiler, Oct 2026 source-available MAX), the reverse of the 2018-2024 database relicensing wave, as its revenue moved to hosted inference (Modular Cloud) and after a hardware company bought it. Open-sourcing the compiler after the sale suggests openness became a tool for ecosystem adoption across chips rather than a source of direct revenue.
key_takeaway: Modular is an AI-era case of 'closed first, open later': a language and inference stack built under proprietary licences that a chip maker (Qualcomm) bought for a reported $3.9B in July 2026, after which the Mojo compiler went Apache-2.0 and MAX became source-available. The money comes from hosted inference and the strategic value of a cross-hardware software layer, not from the licence; MAX still stops short of OSI open source.

notes: Acquisition price $3.9B comes only from one sentence in Wikipedia's Qualcomm article (citation not visible in the fetched text); Modular and Qualcomm pages fetched state no price. The original announcement date of the deal was not found; completion was announced 2026-07-29.

Funding: $250M third round on 2025-09-24 at $1.6B, led by Thomas Tull's US Innovative Technology fund with DFJ Growth, GV, General Catalyst and Greylock; $380M total across three rounds, so the first two rounds sum to ~$130M (individual amounts not confirmed on fetched pages; the 2023 $100M post URL returned 404).
GitHub repo modular/modular created 2023-04-28; API reports licence NOASSERTION because of the dual Apache-2.0-with-LLVM-exceptions / MAX License split (files split 2026-10-22).
Modular Cloud previously served OpenRouter traffic as 'ModelRun'; pricing is pay-per-token shared endpoints and per-minute dedicated GPUs (ModCon post).
